name: RN1
archetype: In-play two-sided market maker (tennis, esports, US sports)
headline: Runs a large in-play market-making book: resting bids on both sides of live tennis, CS2 and football markets, about $65M of fills a month across 28,000 markets. It pulls quotes within seconds of game events. A maker without that speed, using public data, loses 8-19% of capital deployed in the same markets.
mechanism: 92% of sampled fills are maker fills (on-chain, 95% CI 88-95%); 97% happen after game start. Pairs are bought at a median combined 0.98, locking +$964k of spread in 30 days, while the unmatched residual loses $319k to adverse selection. Around ESPN scoring plays, only 2.6% of its passive fills land in the 10 s after a play versus 9.7% for other makers, whose fills in that window lose 26-29%: RN1 cancels quotes within seconds of events.

roc.detail: peak capital at risk $1.14M; 30-day PnL $907k; 79% per month

match.detail: quote pulling after plays observed (2.6% vs 9.7% of passive fills in 0-10 s), but no public-data quoting rule reproduces its fills; most volume is tennis/esports with no public event feed

backtest.detail: public-data two-sided maker on 70 held-out RN1 markets: -7.8% (0 s), -11.7% (2 s), -12.2% (5 s), -18.9% (30 s); RN1's own passive fills there +6.5%

replicable.detail: requires cancelling quotes within seconds of live events; stale passive fills right after scoring plays lose 26-29% for other makers

reasons: A slow two-sided maker with public data loses money in the same markets at every tested delay (0-30 s).
RN1's edge depends on pulling quotes within seconds of live events, which needs low-latency sports and esports data.
No public-data rule reproduces its quoting at the required significance.
